proposal.problem: Students in the Computer Engineering department revise from the lecture PDFs each course publishes on CATS. A fourth-year student typically takes five or six courses, and each course publishes around 10 to 14 slide decks and notes per term, so a single student revises from roughly 60 to 80 PDFs and several hundred pages. To find where a concept such as third normal form or a Fourier transform property is explained, students open files one by one and use the viewer's word search, which only finds exact words and misses slides that explain the idea in other terms. Classmates we talked to estimated that, in exam weeks, finding the right slide for one question takes about 5 to 10 minutes. General chatbots answer quickly but do not use the course's own material, mix in other definitions, and cannot show which slide an answer comes from, so students cannot trust them for the exam. Our earlier prototype indexes only one PDF placed in a folder, must be re-run by hand for every new file, and returns one matching paragraph without a generated answer or a page reference.
proposal.title: CourseGraph: a knowledge-graph assistant that answers questions from course PDFs with cited sources
proposal.mission: Give every Course student and Study group lead at İKÜ a local assistant that turns their course PDFs into a knowledge graph of documents, pages and topics, answers their questions only from that graph with the page each statement comes from, and refuses when the documents do not cover the question.
proposal.outcome: A student uploads the PDFs of a course from one web page, asks a question in their own words and, within seconds, reads an answer whose every part links to the document and page it came from; when the material does not cover the question, the assistant says so instead of guessing.

proposal.techWhy: RDFLib stores every document, page and chunk as RDF triples, so a chunk always knows its document, page and course. A SKOS concept scheme holds each course's topics and links them to chunks. SHACL shapes, run with pySHACL, refuse a file whose pages have no text or whose chunks miss a page number, so the assistant never cites a broken source. SPARQL selects the candidate chunks of the chosen course and topic before embedding similarity ranks them, which is the GraphRAG pattern. PROV-O records which chunks, model and question produced each answer, so any answer can be traced back.

proposal.spec: The system lets a student upload course PDFs from a web page, extracts the text of every page, splits pages into chunks, computes an embedding for each chunk and stores documents, pages, chunks and topics in an RDF graph validated by SHACL shapes. For each question it selects candidate chunks with SPARQL by course and topic, ranks them by embedding similarity, sends the top three to a local LLM through Ollama and returns an answer with the document and page of each cited chunk. It records every answer with PROV-O. When no chunk is similar enough it says that the documents do not cover the question and gives no answer.

scenarios.text: Given a lecture PDF that explains normalization is uploaded, when the student asks what third normal form is, then the answer cites the document and pages of the three chunks it used

Given a scanned PDF with no text layer, when the student uploads it, then the file is refused and the message says it contains no text

proposal.activity: The student opens the page and uploads a PDF. The system extracts its text; if a page has no text the file is refused with a message. Otherwise it splits pages into chunks, computes embeddings, links chunks to topics and validates the graph with SHACL; on a violation the upload is rolled back and reported. The student chooses a course and asks a question. The retriever selects and ranks chunks; if none is similar enough the assistant says no source was found. Otherwise the LLM writes an answer from the top three chunks, citations are attached, the answer is recorded with PROV-O and shown.
proposal.sequence: The web page sends the question and course to the answer service. The answer service sends a SPARQL query to the graph store and receives the candidate chunks of that course. It asks the embedding model for the question vector, ranks the candidates and keeps the top three. It sends the question and the three chunks to Ollama and receives the draft answer. It writes a PROV-O record to the graph and returns the answer with document titles and page numbers to the web page, which shows each citation as a link to the page.

proposal.classModel: Document has a course code, a title, a file fingerprint and many Pages. Page has a page number and text and belongs to one Document. Chunk has text, an embedding and a position and belongs to one Page; a Chunk may discuss several Topics. Topic is a skos:Concept in the course's concept scheme. Question has a text and a chosen course. Answer has a text, a model name and many Citations, and is a prov:Entity generated from one Question. Citation links an Answer to one Chunk.

proposal.model_Architecture: Design-level class diagram: Document, Page, Chunk, Topic (skos:Concept), Question, Answer (prov:Entity) and Citation as in the class model; DocumentShape requires a course code and at least one Page, PageShape requires non-empty text and a page number, ChunkShape requires a Page and an embedding.
proposal.model_Data: Component diagram: WebPage (Flask) calls IngestService and AnswerService; IngestService uses PyPDF, the embedding model and Validator (pySHACL) and writes to GraphStore (RDFLib); AnswerService queries GraphStore with SPARQL, calls the embedding model and the local LLM through Ollama, and writes PROV-O records; Evaluator runs the question set through AnswerService.
proposal.model_Interaction: Sequence of an upload: the student drops a PDF on the page; the page sends it to IngestService; IngestService extracts the text, builds pages and chunks, validates them and either stores them and returns ready, or rolls back and returns the reason; the page updates the document's status.
proposal.model_User_interface: One page in three parts: an upload area listing each document with its course and status (ready or refused with the reason); a question box with a course filter and the answer below it, each citation shown as document title and page number; a report tab with Recall@3, citation accuracy and median answer time.

proposal.libraries: Python libraries: PyPDF for text extraction, sentence-transformers for embeddings, RDFLib and pySHACL for the graph and its validation, Flask for the web page, the ollama client for the local model, and pytest for tests. Course topics applied: files and paths (pathlib) for the document folder, regular expressions to clean extracted text and read course codes from file names, reading PDF documents, web pages with Flask, multithreading to index several PDFs at once, and openpyxl to export the evaluation results.
